chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the dove and what resembles it: when the one in Ihram kills it, (he must offer) a sheep; and if it was chicks, he must equate them from the lambs.

And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who trod on an ostrich egg and broke it while he was in Ihram: Ali (peace be upon him) judged that he should send a male camel to match the number of the eggs among the camels; whatever gets pregnant and remains safe until it gives birth, the offspring is an offering that reaches the Ka'bah.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing birds or breaking eggs while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the fidyah (expiation) for breaking the sanctity of Ihram by killing birds or eggs, reflecting the juristic principle of 'adl' (equivalence) in compensation. It highlights the unique ruling for ostrich eggs, where the offspring of camels serve as the sacrificial offering, illustrating the practical application of Imam Ali’s (AS) legal reasoning in early Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said regarding the dove and what resembles it: ‘When the one in Ihraam kills it, (upon him would be) a sheep; and if it was a chick, so he would equate it from the lambs’.

And heasws said regarding a man trampling an ostrich egg, so he breaks it, and he is in Ihraam, so heasws said: ‘Aliasws judged with regards to it that he should send the stallion upon a similar number of the eggs, to be among the camels. So whatever gets impregnated and is safe until it is produced, the produced would be an offering to reach the Kabah’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
For killing pigeons and the like in the state of Ihram, the ransom is one sheep, and for chicks it is one lamb for each.’

He (the Imam) about a man who steps on the eggs of ostrich and breaks, has said, ‘Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, issued a judgment that said, “He must send male camel on female camel equal to the number of eggs affected and whatever the product is, as offering, it must rich al-Ka‘bah as offering.’”
